title: REST API Development
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of rest api development using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates rest api development.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **REST API Development** as part of **Kotlin for Backend and Server-Side Development**. A server endpoint should validate input, apply authorization at the server boundary, return consistent status codes, and be covered by tests and operational monitoring. Use the subtopics—Resource-Based API Design, Request Validation, Error Responses and Status Codes—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Backend code handles untrusted requests and persistent data. Validation, authorization, predictable errors, and operational checks must happen on the server.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A server endpoint should validate input, apply authorization at the server boundary, return consistent status codes, and be covered by tests and operational monitoring.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with resource-based api design. Then compare it with request validation. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Resource-Based API Design
items.text: Resource-Based API Design crosses a system boundary. Model success and failure, validate external data, apply timeout/retry rules deliberately, and keep credentials and database access out of presentation code.

items.title: Request Validation
items.text: Request Validation defines a trust boundary. Validate untrusted input at the boundary, keep secrets server-side, check authorization where the protected operation occurs, and test both allowed and rejected cases.

items.title: Error Responses and Status Codes
items.text: Error Responses and Status Codes is one part of rest api development. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: REST API Development removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
